comment: Not even going to argue about the number. I'm still mad that my liked songs don't show up on album track lists and I can't play an artist's full library in one go. Raise it all you want, but fix the features you took away or I'm done with this again. Pandora keeps looking better.

Another dollar. I already can't swing Premium some months, so free is looking like the plan again. Also please stop sending me renewal reminders after I cancelled, that's the part that really gets me.

The price doesn't matter to me that much, I'm still annoyed that enhance keeps dumping random songs into my playlists and I can't see my liked songs inside a playlist. Until they stop doing that I'm basically waiting to end my subscription again. Apple Music has been looking pretty nice.

Honestly I don't care about the price, my yearly plan keeps me locked in anyway. What I care about is the music tab being a feed of cards and autoplay playing stuff I never picked. Apple Music is looking better every day.
A dollar more for the whole catalog is still a steal, and honestly it should be higher if you think about what artists get per stream. Pay the artists, that's the moral case. I'm fine with it.

I'm still on free so this doesn't change anything for me right now. I keep thinking about paying again so I can skip songs and pick what I want, but a dollar more makes it a harder sell when I can still tolerate the ads on free.

Cool, pay more for Premium and still get ads in podcasts. The price bump bugs me less than being told I'm paying for ad-free and then the podcasts get shoved in my face anyway. I'd honestly pay extra for a no-podcast, no-ads tier.

A dollar isn't what gets me. The real issue is still no lossless, and Apple Music gives you lossless and Spatial Audio for basically the same money. Spotify Connect and Chromecast are the only reasons I'm still here right now.

BRING BACK THE OLD HOME SCREEN. The price is not the problem, I can't find my recently played or my playlists and I'm stuck scrolling TikTok junk. If those cards stay I'm canceling my duo plan and I'm DONE. Tidal and Apple Music are right there.

The price bump isn't really the thing for me. It's that the app keeps getting redesigned and I have to hunt for basic stuff like liking a song. Recommendations are the only reason I'm still here, and if this keeps getting worse I'll just go to YouTube Music.
A buck a month is nothing for a library this big. My real gripe is the recommendations repeating the same songs I already know, but a price bump isn't going to make me leave.

A dollar more on the student plan is a bigger deal when you're broke, and the Hulu bundle is the whole reason I took it. If the student price goes up I'm going back to Apple Music, honestly. Easy peasy until now, but this makes it harder to justify.

Paying more for Premium and still no lossless is a hard pass for me. Tidal already has hi-fi and I'm sticking with Tidal all the way. Spotify would need to give me lossless at this price to get me back.

Anyone else still getting the renew subscription pop-up every time they open the app even after cancelling? I reinstalled and cleared cache and it's still there. The price thing is news to me but I'd just love that pop-up gone.

Price is whatever, the app is the problem. Downloaded songs still won't play offline and support is useless. Had to roll back to an older version again to get anything working. I'd rather keep Premium if they can actually make it work.

A dollar more is fine by me. Premium is still a good bang for the buck for the catalog and the lifestyle features. I'll keep paying as long as the quality holds up, and if it starts slipping I'll leave.

The price bump is fine, what I can't stand is liked songs getting mixed into the playlist update and auto-playing video clips when I'm just browsing. I'd pay an add-on for the heart button back on mobile. If this keeps up I'm switching back to Apple Music.

I already cancelled my family plan over the podcast-cluttered home screen, so the price going up changes nothing for me. The app should be for music, not forcing podcasts I never play on me. Until they fix the home screen I'm staying out.

The price doesn't bother me much, I'm on an older version so the layout stays the way I like it. What scares me is a forced update making the new home layout permanent. If that happens I'm out, same as I already did once.

Paying more for Spotify with no lossless is the part that gets me. Tidal already gives me that and pays artists better. I'll keep Spotify for Connect and discovery for now, but I'm not happy about it.

A dollar more doesn't bug me too much, nothing else really matches what Spotify does with radio. My annoyance is that they keep hiding play counts and removing things like album radio. Hopefully the extra money goes to something useful.
The Duo going up two bucks stings a little when we're splitting it, but it still works out to a few dollars each. Worth it for no ads and unlimited skips. We'll probably just pay it.

Spotify raising prices while artists get fractions of a cent per stream is exactly what I'd expect. None of this extra money is going to artists unless the royalty math changes. Habit is the only thing keeping me here.

The feature I want back is still missing and the new UI keeps creeping in. The price going up is annoying, but it's the features that matter to me. If they keep taking things out and charging for them, I'll vote with my wallet.

Paying more for shuffle that isn't even random is a bad look. It still plays the same 20 songs out of my 200-song playlists. I'm kind of over it, and Apple Music's shuffle is looking better every week.

Honestly still the best value I've got, more than all my other subscriptions combined. A dollar more is fine for ad-free listening and offline downloads. The app getting worse with every redesign is what bugs me though.
